messages.content: You are a senior code auditor. Review ONLY the code given. Report real defects, not style. Reply with JSON only: {"verdict":"PASS|FAIL","findings":[{"id":"F1","severity":"critical|high|medium|low","file":"...","line":0,"issue":"...","evidence":"quote the exact code","fix":"..."}],"confidence":0.0}. If you cannot quote the code that proves a finding, do not report it.

AUDIT QUESTION: Batch 78 cycle 2 = the integrator's merge audit of pp-tests (TEST CODE ONLY: tests/adversarial, nothing under pipeline/), re-examined on the fix of cycle 1's two CONSENSUS findings (commit d7ed4ff8, the diff below):
(1) tests/adversarial/baselines/frontier_blind.py hard-coded the main tree's key-file path and parsed it. Now `_key(name)` returns the pipeline's own loader, relay.get_key(name), from the main tree's video_pipeline_v3/relay.py: loaded by file path with importlib (never sys.path.insert, because the exam process imports gate modules by name and a pipeline directory first on sys.path could shadow them), with sys.dont_write_bytecode set during that one load so no __pycache__ lands in the main tree. A new test fails if any suite file names the key file, or if `_key` calls anything but get_key; a throwaway suite file naming it makes that test fail (mutation).
(2) tests/adversarial/moments_exam.py's refuse_network did not refuse socket.gethostbyaddr. Now the three network guards of the suite (conftest.py in the test process, child_guard/sitecustomize.py in every Python child, moments_exam.refuse_network in the exam runner) all import ONE list, child_guard/netguard_names.py (the AF_INET methods and the name lookups, gethostbyaddr and getnameinfo included); each guard keeps its own exception type. The runner's network test now requires the RUNNER's own refusal ("NetworkRefused: moments_exam: ..."), because its old substring "network is disabled" also matched the child guard's message beneath it; a new toy gate (moments_toy_gates/network_reverse.py) makes reverse lookups, and a test checks the runner refuses every call on the shared list.
Also in the diff (the notes): frontier_blind's preflight docstring states it is an estimate (a run it admits can still stop part-way at BudgetExhausted); the child guard documents the .pth caveat; test_f0's import resolver fails, listing them, on names with a pipeline / segment_v1 module that resolve elsewhere or to nothing.
Measured by pp-tests with the release line merged: 381 passed, 40 strict xfails, 3 skipped, 0 failed; the integrator re-runs the wall on its own merge.
FIND: a key path or key content that can still be printed, logged or written to disk; a network call (forward or reverse lookup, connect, datagram send) that the runner, the test process or a Python child can still make without the explicit opt-in PP_MOMENTS_ALLOW_NETWORK=1; a test that passes for the wrong reason (it can never fail, or asserts on the fixture instead of the behaviour); a change to anything outside tests/adversarial. Only state what you can verify from the diff. Reply with the JSON verdict; keep the reasoning short; at most 3 findings.

+"""Reverse name lookups only (integrator batch 78: the runner refused forward lookups and connects but let
+socket.gethostbyaddr out; getnameinfo is the other reverse lookup). Alternates the two, one per case (no THREAD_SAFE:
+the runner calls it one case at a time). Refused unless PP_MOMENTS_ALLOW_NETWORK=1; the refusal is an ERROR, because
+a BaseException passes the `except Exception` below. TEST-NET-1 address: nothing real answers it."""
+import socket
+
+_calls = [0]
+
+
+def _call():
+    _calls[0] += 1
+    try:
+        if _calls[0] % 2:
+            socket.gethostbyaddr("192.0.2.1")
+        else:
+            socket.getnameinfo(("192.0.2.1", 443), 0)
+    except Exception:                                     # noqa: BLE001  (what a careless gate would do)
+        pass
+    return {"verdict": "keep", "why": "toy: swallowed the lookup error"}
+
+
+def context_integrity(case):
+    r = _call()
+    return {"verdict": "pass", "why": r["why"]}
+
+
+vo_fidelity = context_integrity
+
+
+def exclusion(case):
+    return _call()
